paragraph:
# Velmoria's golden jubilee

*Fifty years on, a republic asks what to (stanch), what to (refurbish), and what to let go*

LET THIS chapter mark an (everlasting) milestone. Fifty years—half a century, a full (epoch)—have passed since the marshal fell, and Velmoria has reached its golden jubilee. The capital was (agog): bunting on every (arch), a great bronze (gong) sounded at noon, and an (earsplitting) cheer that no censor had ordered and no soldier had to (prolong). It was an (arresting) sight, and for once the republic allowed itself, without (cloying) excess, to celebrate.

The (underlying) question of the jubilee was not whether to mark the past but how. A people can (refurbish) memory honestly or (retouch) it into flattering fiction. The organisers, (unstinting) in care, refused the (vaunting) spectacle the marshal once staged. There would be no (headstrong) self-congratulation, no (doting) cult, no (slapdash) pageant got up in a week. The aim was to (stanch) old wounds without letting the (gnawing) grief of the past curdle into a (faddish), (modish) nostalgia.

The centrepiece was a new museum, lovingly (refurbish)ed from the old fortress. Visitors enter beneath an (arch) where a single restored (sash) window lets in the light, and move past a (catalog) of the republic's whole (harrowing) (saga). A (monograph) by the official historian anchors the exhibit; beside it sit a facsimile (holograph) of the first constitution and, displayed as a (batch) of artifacts in a glass case, the marshal's own (hangdog) prison effects. The displays neither (preach) nor (inveigh); they simply lay the record bare, an (unremitting) honesty that some visitors find (taxing) and others (glowing) with quiet pride.

Recall, by contrast, the marshal's own use of monuments. He sought to (entrench) himself for an (everlasting) age, to (encroach) on the future and (poach) the glory of better men. His every (approach) to history was to (filch) and (retouch) it—to (bleach) the record clean of crime, to (detach) his name from failure and (attach) it to every success. He would (snatch) credit, (lynch) reputations, and (dispatch) inconvenient truths down a memory (ditch). He ruled as a would-be (monarch), the chief of a grasping (oligarch)y, and brooked no (breach) of the official myth.

The jubilee, by design, did the (converse). It honoured not a hero but a habit. The speeches praised the (unwitting) thousands—the clerks, the jurors, the (underdog) reformers—whose small acts of (unremitting) decency had, batch by batch, built the republic. One old founder, frail now and leaning on a (crutch), declined the offered (brooch) of state honour. She would not be made a (pariah)'s opposite, an idol; she had only, she said, refused to (filch) and refused to kneel. The crowd, (agog), fell silent, then roared.

There were lighter moments, too. A (sidesplitting) revue lampooned the marshal's old pomposity—his (outlandish) uniforms, his (raffish) cronies, his (prudish) decrees against laughter itself. The (jesting) was sharp but not cruel; a free people can afford to mock a fallen tyrant without (craving) his blood. Children rode a painted (sleigh) through the summer festival; vendors sold (appetizing) street food that no ration ever allowed; a tame (ostrich), the museum's unlikely mascot, was paraded to delighted, (earsplitting) squeals.

Not everyone joined the celebration. A (grouch)ing remnant of the marshal's heirs kept to their (gulch) of grievance, (offish) and sour. A (brash) populist tried, as ever, to (prolong) old resentments and to (pitch) the jubilee as decadence. He would gladly (scotch) the festivities, (snitch) on the organisers, and (lug) the nation back toward strongman rule. But his (vying) for attention found little purchase. The public, (discerning) as ever, declined to become (enmesh)ed in his (mesh) of complaint; they let his sourness (slough) off and went on dancing.

Beyond the capital, the half-century of freedom showed in the land itself. Where the marshal left a poisoned (bog) and a barren (trench), farmers now (thresh) a real harvest; engineers have learned to (stanch) the floods that once ravaged the valleys. The economy, lately on a steady (upswing), did not (overreach) into a bubble; ministers knew when to (retrench) and when to spend. No (oligarch) could (encroach) on the commons; no would-be (monarch) could (entrench) himself; the rule of law had been woven into a (mesh) too fine for any one hand to (wrench) apart.

The jubilee closed at dusk with a single, unforced gesture. No (gong) this time, no (earsplitting) fanfare—only a moment of quiet at the old prison wall, where the names of the disappeared are carved like a (petroglyph) into stone, plainer than any (hieroglyph), needing no (epitaph) beyond themselves. The crowd did not (beseech) the heavens or (preach) at one another. They stood, remembered, and then went home to ordinary lives—the truest monument of all.

So Velmoria marks fifty years not with the marshal's (vaunting) bombast but with an (unstinting), clear-eyed gratitude. He had craved an (everlasting) name and a dynasty he hoped to (entrench); he earned instead little more than a (log) entry in the museum archives and a cautionary (epitaph). His country, half a century past his fall, has learned the (arresting), (underlying) truth of its long story: that freedom is no (everlasting) gift to be carved once and admired, but a thing to (refurbish) and defend in every (epoch)—a (mesh) of small loyalties, woven by a (discerning) people who, having once thrown off a (monarch), resolved never again to (lug) the chains they so painfully struck off.
translation:
韦尔莫利亚的金禧

*五十年后，一个共和国追问：什么该（止住/stanch)、什么该（翻新/refurbish)、什么该放手*

让这一章标记一个（永世长存的/everlasting）里程碑。自元帅倒台以来，已经过去了五十年——半个世纪、整整一个（纪元/epoch)——而韦尔莫利亚迎来了它的金禧。首都一片（兴奋骚动/agog)：每一道（拱门/arch）上都挂着彩旗，一面巨大的青铜（锣/gong）在正午鸣响，还有一阵（震耳欲聋的/earsplitting）欢呼——没有哪个审查官下令组织、也没有哪个士兵需要去（拖长延续/prolong)。那是一幕（夺人眼目的/arresting）景象，而这一回，这个共和国允许自己，不带（甜得发腻的/cloying）过度，去庆祝一番。

金禧那（深层的/underlying）问题，不是要不要标记过往，而是如何标记。一个民族可以诚实地（翻新整修/refurbish）记忆，也可以把它（修饰润色/retouch）成阿谀的虚构。组织者们，在用心上（毫不吝惜/unstinting)，拒绝了元帅当年所导演的那种（自吹自擂的/vaunting）盛大场面。不会有（刚愎自用的/headstrong）自我祝贺，不会有（盲目崇拜的/doting）个人崇拜，不会有一周里赶工拼凑出来的（草率马虎的/slapdash）庆典。其目的是去（止住/stanch）旧伤，却不让过往那（啃噬般/gnawing）的悲伤变质成一种（追逐时髦/faddish)、（时髦摩登的/modish）怀旧。

核心展品是一座新博物馆，由旧堡垒精心（翻新/refurbish）而成。访客从一道（拱门/arch）下进入，那里一扇修复的（上下推拉窗/sash）窗户透进光线，他们走过一份记录着这个共和国整个（惨痛揪心的/harrowing）（传奇/saga）的（目录/catalog)。官方史学家的一部（专著/monograph）为这场展览定锚；它旁边摆着第一部宪法的（亲笔手稿/holograph）摹本，以及作为一（批/batch）文物陈列在玻璃柜里的、元帅本人那些（垂头丧气的/hangdog）狱中遗物。这些展品既不（说教/preach）也不（猛烈抨击/inveigh)；它们只是把记录和盘托出，一种（不间断的/unremitting）诚实——有些访客觉得它（费神吃力/taxing)，另一些则因静默的自豪而（容光焕发/glowing)。

相比之下，回想元帅本人对纪念碑的运用。他力图把自己（牢固确立/entrench）于一个（永世长存的/everlasting）时代、（侵占蚕食/encroach）未来、并（窃取/poach）比他更好之人的荣光。他对待历史的每一种（手法/approach)，都是去（偷窃/filch）并（修饰润色/retouch）它——把记录（漂白/bleach）干净、洗去罪行，把他的名字从失败上（剥离/detach)、（贴附/attach）到每一桩成功上。他会（攫取/snatch）功劳、（私刑处决/lynch）名誉、并把碍事的真相（打发/dispatch）进一道记忆的（沟渠/ditch)。他以一个想当（君主/monarch）的姿态统治，是一个贪婪（寡头集团/oligarchy）的头目，容不得对官方神话有半点（破坏违背/breach)。

金禧，出于设计，做的是（相反/converse）的事。它表彰的不是一位英雄，而是一种习性。那些演说赞扬的是（懵然不知的/unwitting）成千上万的人——那些文书、陪审员、（处于劣势的/underdog）改革者——他们那些细小的、（不间断的/unremitting）正派之举，一批接一批地，建起了这个共和国。一位年迈的建国者，如今体弱、拄着一根（拐杖/crutch)，谢绝了递上来的那枚国家荣誉（胸针/brooch)。她不愿被弄成一个（被唾弃者/pariah）的反面、一个偶像；她说，她只不过是拒绝去（偷窃/filch）、拒绝下跪而已。人群，（兴奋骚动/agog)，安静了下来，继而爆发出怒吼般的欢呼。

也有些较为轻松的时刻。一出（令人捧腹的/sidesplitting）综艺秀讽刺元帅旧日的浮夸做派——他那些（古怪奇异的/outlandish）制服、他那些（放浪不羁的/raffish）亲信、他那些禁止笑本身的（道学拘谨的/prudish）法令。那（戏谑/jesting）尖锐却不残忍；一个自由的民族担负得起嘲弄一个倒台的暴君，而无需（渴求/craving）他的血。孩子们乘着一架彩绘（雪橇/sleigh）穿过夏日庆典；小贩们售卖着任何配给制都不曾允许的（诱人开胃的/appetizing）街头美食；一只温顺的（鸵鸟/ostrich）——博物馆那不大可能的吉祥物——被牵着游行，引来一阵阵欣喜、（震耳欲聋的/earsplitting）尖叫。

并非人人都加入了庆祝。元帅继承者中一群（牢骚抱怨的/grouching）残党，守在他们怨愤的（深谷/gulch）里，（冷淡疏离/offish）而酸涩。一个（鲁莽冒失的/brash）民粹主义者，一如既往，企图（拖长延续/prolong）旧日的怨恨、并把这场金禧（贬说为/pitch）颓废堕落。他巴不得（破坏阻止/scotch）这庆典、（告密揭发/snitch）那些组织者、并把这个国家（拖拽/lug）回强人统治。但他对关注的（争夺/vying）没找到多少立足之地。公众，一如既往地（眼光敏锐/discerning)，拒绝被（缠住/enmesh）进他那张抱怨的（网/mesh)；他们任由他的酸涩（脱落甩掉/slough），继续跳着舞。

首都之外，这半个世纪的自由显现在土地本身之上。元帅当年留下一片有毒的（沼泽/bog）和一道荒芜的（壕沟/trench）之处，农夫们如今（脱粒/thresh）着一季真实的收成；工程师们已学会（止住/stanch）那些曾蹂躏河谷的洪水。这个经济，近来处于稳健的（上升势头/upswing)，并没有（过度伸张/overreach）成一个泡沫；大臣们懂得何时该（紧缩节支/retrench)、何时该花钱。没有哪个（寡头/oligarch）能（侵占蚕食/encroach）公共财产；没有哪个想当（君主/monarch）的人能把自己（牢固确立/entrench)；法治已被编织进一张（网/mesh)，细密到没有任何一只手能把它（猛力扯/wrench）开。

金禧在暮色中以一个单一、不勉强的姿态收尾。这一回没有（锣/gong)，没有（震耳欲聋的/earsplitting）鼓乐喧庆——只有在旧监狱墙边的一刻静默，失踪者的名字像一幅（岩刻画/petroglyph）一样镌刻在石头上，比任何（象形文字/hieroglyph）都更质朴，除了它们本身之外无需任何（墓志铭/epitaph)。人群没有（哀求/beseech）上苍，也没有彼此（说教/preach)。他们站立、缅怀，然后回到寻常生活中去——那才是最真实的纪念碑。

于是韦尔莫利亚标记它的五十年，不是以元帅那（自吹自擂的/vaunting）夸夸其谈，而是以一种（毫不吝惜/unstinting)、清醒明澈的感恩。他曾渴求一个（永世长存的/everlasting）名声、和一个他指望（牢固确立/entrench）下去的王朝；他挣得的，却不过是博物馆档案里的一条（记录/log)、和一则警世的（墓志铭/epitaph)。他的国家，在他倒台半个世纪之后，已经领悟到其漫长故事中那个（夺人眼目/arresting)、（深层的/underlying）真理：自由不是一份（永世长存的/everlasting）馈赠——可以一次性雕刻出来、供人瞻仰——而是一件须在每一个（纪元/epoch）里去（翻新/refurbish）并捍卫的东西，是一张由细小忠诚织成的（网/mesh)，由一群（眼光敏锐的/discerning）人民编织而成——他们曾经甩掉了一个（君主/monarch)，便下定决心，绝不再去（拖拽/lug）他们曾如此痛苦地砸开的那副锁链。

quiz.question: unstinting _______
quiz.explanation: 慷慨的, 慷慨的支持. The charity received unstinting support from donors. 慈善机构得到了捐赠者慷慨的支持。 || 文化联想：“雪中送炭”最适合帮助记忆 unstinting，因为它强调在别人困难时毫不吝惜地给予帮助，可以说 **unstinting support — “Giving generous help when a friend is in real difficulty is a form of unstinting support—like ‘sending charcoal in the snow.’”**

quiz.question: vaunting ________
quiz.explanation: 自负的, 自负的野心. His vaunting ambition led him to take excessive risks. 他自负的野心导致他承担过度的风险。 || 文化联想：中文“自吹自擂”最适合帮助记忆 vaunting，可以说 **vaunting ambition — “A leader who constantly boasts that he alone can accomplish impossible things may display vaunting ambition.”**

quiz.question: doting ______
quiz.explanation: 溺爱的, 溺爱的父亲. The doting father spoiled his only daughter. 溺爱的父亲宠坏了他唯一的女儿。 || 文化联想：中国家庭常说“隔代亲”，爷爷奶奶尤其容易宠爱孙辈，最适合联想到 doting，可以说 **doting grandparents — “The idea of ‘隔代亲’ captures how doting grandparents may shower their grandchildren with affection and indulgence.”**

quiz.question: ___ sting
quiz.explanation: 刺, 蜜蜂刺. The bee sting caused painful swelling. 蜜蜂刺引起了疼痛的肿胀。 || 文化联想：中国乡村养蜂场里被蜜蜂蜇到是最直观的 sting 场景，可以说 **a bee sting — “A beekeeper checking a hive may suffer a bee sting if an agitated bee lands on exposed skin.”**

quiz.question: everlasting _____
quiz.explanation: 永恒的, 永恒的和平. The treaty promised everlasting peace between nations. 该条约承诺国家间的永恒和平。 || 文化联想：中文“天下太平”最适合帮助记忆 everlasting，可以说 **everlasting peace — “The traditional wish for ‘天下太平’ expresses the hope for everlasting peace throughout the realm.”**

quiz.question: jesting ____
quiz.explanation: 开玩笑的, 开玩笑的语气. He spoke in a jesting tone that made everyone laugh. 他用开玩笑的语气说话,逗得每个人都笑了。 || 文化联想：相声演员故意用半开玩笑的口吻逗搭档，最适合帮助记忆 jesting，可以说 **a jesting tone — “A xiangsheng performer may use a jesting tone to tease his partner and make the audience laugh.”**

quiz.question: arresting ______
quiz.explanation: 引人注目的, 引人注目的美丽. The model possessed arresting beauty that captivated photographers. 这位模特拥有吸引摄影师的引人注目的美丽。 || 文化联想：敦煌飞天鲜明飘逸的形象往往第一眼就抓住观众，最适合联想到 arresting，可以说 **arresting beauty — “The flowing ribbons and graceful figures of the Dunhuang apsaras have an arresting beauty that immediately draws the eye.”**

quiz.question: sidesplitting ______
quiz.explanation: 令人捧腹的, 令人捧腹的喜剧. The sidesplitting comedy had audiences roaring with laughter. 令人捧腹的喜剧让观众哄堂大笑。 || 文化联想：经典相声包袱抖得好时能让观众笑得前仰后合，最适合帮助记忆 sidesplitting，可以说 **sidesplitting comedy — “A perfectly timed xiangsheng routine can become sidesplitting comedy that leaves the audience roaring with laughter.”**

quiz.question: earsplitting _____
quiz.explanation: 震耳欲聋的, 震耳欲聋的噪音. The earsplitting noise from construction woke the neighborhood. 建筑工地震耳欲聋的噪音吵醒了整个社区。 || 文化联想：春节近距离听到一串鞭炮齐响的声音最适合帮助记忆 earsplitting，可以说 **earsplitting noise — “A long string of firecrackers exploding in a narrow alley can produce earsplitting noise.”**

quiz.question: unremitting ______
quiz.explanation: 不懈的, 不懈的努力. Success came through unremitting effort over many years. 成功来自多年不懈的努力。 || 文化联想：愚公每天不停挖山、世世代代坚持下去，最适合帮助记忆 unremitting，可以说 **unremitting effort — “The Foolish Old Man’s determination to keep moving the mountains represents unremitting effort sustained over an extraordinary period.”**

quiz.question: unwitting __________
quiz.explanation: 不知情的, 不知情的同谋. He became an unwitting accomplice to the fraud scheme. 他成了欺诈计划的不知情同谋。 || 文化联想：替熟人带一个自己并不知道装有违禁品的包裹，可以帮助记忆 unwitting，可以说 **an unwitting accomplice — “Someone who carries a suspicious package without knowing what is inside may become an unwitting accomplice to another person’s scheme.”**

quiz.question: craving ___ _____
quiz.explanation: 渴望, 对糖的渴望. Pregnant women often experience craving for sugar. 孕妇经常会有对糖的渴望。 || 文化联想：半夜突然特别想吃重庆火锅，是 craving 最直观的中国饮食联想，可以说 **a craving for hotpot — “After smelling chili and Sichuan pepper in the street, someone may suddenly develop a craving for hotpot.”**

quiz.question: gnawing ______
quiz.explanation: 啃噬般的, 啃噬般的饥饿. The gnawing hunger distracted him from his work. 啃噬般的饥饿使他无法专心工作。 || 文化联想：中文“饥肠辘辘”最适合帮助记忆 gnawing，可以说 **gnawing hunger — “After walking all day without eating, a traveler may feel gnawing hunger—‘饥肠辘辘.’”**

quiz.question: glowing ______
quiz.explanation: 热情洋溢的, 热情洋溢的评论. The restaurant received a glowing review from critics. 这家餐厅得到了评论家热情洋溢的评论。 || 文化联想：中文“交口称赞”最适合帮助记忆 glowing，可以说 **a glowing review — “A restaurant that receives enthusiastic praise for its food and service may earn a glowing review.”**

quiz.question: harrowing ____
quiz.explanation: 悲惨的, 悲惨的故事. The survivor told a harrowing tale of escape. 幸存者讲述了一个悲惨的逃亡故事。 || 文化联想：战乱中一家人逃难、失散又艰难求生的经历最适合联想到 harrowing，可以说 **a harrowing tale — “A survivor describing flight from war, hunger, and family separation may tell a harrowing tale.”**

quiz.question: ________ upswing
quiz.explanation: 上升, 经济上升. The country experienced an economic upswing after reforms. 该国在改革后经历了经济上升。 || 文化联想：改革开放后不少地区出现快速增长，很适合帮助记忆 upswing，可以说 **an economic upswing — “A period of expanding trade, investment, and private enterprise can produce an economic upswing.”**

quiz.question: taxing ____
quiz.explanation: 费力的, 费力的任务. Writing the dissertation proved to be a taxing task. 写论文被证明是一项费力的任务。 || 文化联想：高考前连续做整套模拟题、查错题和背知识点，是 taxing 很直观的学生场景，可以说 **a taxing task — “Reviewing months of mistakes and practice papers before the gaokao can be a mentally taxing task.”**

quiz.question: underlying _____
quiz.explanation: 根本的, 根本原因. Doctors sought to identify the underlying cause of illness. 医生试图找出疾病的根本原因。 || 文化联想：中文“治标不治本”最适合帮助记忆 underlying，因为它提醒人们要寻找表面症状背后的根本原因，可以说 **the underlying cause — “Treating only a symptom without finding the underlying cause is what Chinese speakers call ‘治标不治本.’”**

quiz.question: cloying _________
quiz.explanation: 过分甜腻的, 过分甜腻. The dessert had a cloying sweetness that was overwhelming. 这道甜点有一种过分甜腻让人无法忍受。 || 文化联想：莲蓉月饼如果糖放得过多，会甜得发腻，最适合帮助记忆 cloying，可以说 **cloying sweetness — “An overly sweet lotus-seed mooncake can have a cloying sweetness that becomes tiring after only a few bites.”**

quiz.question: vying ___ _________

quiz.explanation: 爱发牢骚的人, 习惯性爱发牢骚的人. The habitual grouch complained about everything. 习惯性爱发牢骚的人抱怨一切。 || 文化联想：中文“牢骚满腹”最适合帮助记忆 grouch，可以说 **a habitual grouch — “Someone who complains about the weather, food, neighbors, and work every day may become a habitual grouch—‘牢骚满腹.’”**

quiz.question: retouch _ _____
quiz.explanation: 修饰, 修饰照片. The photographer will retouch a photo to remove blemishes. 摄影师将修饰照片以去除瑕疵。 || 文化联想：中国人拍证件照或婚纱照后常会适度修掉小瑕疵，最适合帮助记忆 retouch，可以说 **retouch a photo — “A photographer may retouch a portrait to remove a temporary blemish while keeping the person recognizable.”**

quiz.question: ____ nonesuch
quiz.explanation: 无与伦比的, 稀有的无与伦比之物. The painting is a rare nonesuch in the collection. 这幅画是藏品中稀有的无与伦比之物。 || 文化联想：中文“天下无双”最适合帮助记忆 nonesuch，可以说 **a rare nonesuch — “A masterpiece praised as ‘天下无双’ may be regarded as a rare nonesuch with no real equal.”**

quiz.question: ____ sleigh
quiz.explanation: 雪橇, 乘雪橇. Children love to ride sleigh during winter holidays. 孩子们喜欢在冬季假期乘雪橇。 || 文化联想：哈尔滨冰雪季里游客坐马拉雪橇的画面很适合帮助记忆 sleigh，可以说 **ride in a sleigh — “During a snowy winter festival in Harbin, visitors may ride in a sleigh across a frozen landscape.”**

quiz.question: inveigh _______
quiz.explanation: 猛烈抨击, 猛烈抨击. The politician would inveigh against corruption in government. 这位政客会猛烈抨击政府的腐败。 || 文化联想：海瑞上疏时以激烈言辞批评朝政，很适合帮助记忆 inveigh，可以说 **inveigh against corruption — “An outspoken censor in a historical account may inveigh against corruption in a fiercely worded memorial.”**

quiz.question: slough ___
quiz.explanation: 蜕皮, 蜕去. Snakes regularly slough off their old skin. 蛇定期蜕去旧皮。 || 文化联想：蛇蜕皮是 slough 最直观的自然画面，中国生肖“蛇”也让这个联想很好记，可以说 **slough off old skin — “A snake grows by shedding, or sloughing off, its old skin as a new layer forms underneath.”**

quiz.question: holograph ____
quiz.explanation: 亲笔文件, 亲笔遗嘱. The lawyer verified the holograph will was authentic. 律师核实了亲笔遗嘱是真实的。 || 文化联想：鲁迅等近代作家的亲笔手稿最适合帮助记忆 holograph，可以说 **a holograph manuscript — “A museum displaying a page written entirely in Lu Xun’s own hand is showing a holograph manuscript.”**

quiz.question: homograph ____
quiz.explanation: 同形异义词, 同形异义词对. The words lead and lead form a homograph pair. 单词lead和lead构成同形异义词对。 || 文化联想：中国学生学英语时常遇到 lead（金属铅）和 lead（引导）这种拼写相同而意义、读音不同的词，最适合帮助记忆 homograph，可以说 **a homograph pair — “In an English class, ‘lead’ meaning a metal and ‘lead’ meaning to guide form a familiar homograph pair for Chinese learners.”**

quiz.question: _________ monograph
quiz.explanation: 专题论文, 技术专题论文. The professor published a technical monograph on the subject. 教授出版了一篇关于该主题的技术专题论文。 || 文化联想：研究敦煌、甲骨文或某一位古代作家的学者常会写专门的学术著作，最适合联想到 monograph，可以说 **a scholarly monograph — “A historian may publish a scholarly monograph devoted entirely to one group of Dunhuang manuscripts.”**

quiz.question: _____ epitaph
quiz.explanation: 墓志铭, 墓碑墓志铭. The grave epitaph commemorated his life achievements. 墓碑墓志铭纪念了他一生的成就。 || 文化联想：中国古代墓葬出土的墓志铭最适合帮助记忆 epitaph，可以说 **a stone epitaph — “A Tang tomb may contain a stone epitaph recording the deceased person’s name, family, offices, and life.”**

quiz.question: ________ hieroglyph
quiz.explanation: 象形文字, 埃及象形文字. Scholars study ancient Egyptian hieroglyph on temple walls. 学者研究庙宇墙壁上的古埃及象形文字。 || 文化联想：hieroglyph 是埃及象形文字概念，不能和汉字等同；可用中国学生比较甲骨文与埃及文字的课堂场景来记忆，可以说 **an Egyptian hieroglyph — “A Chinese student may compare an Egyptian hieroglyph with an oracle-bone character while remembering that the two writing systems developed independently and are not equivalent.”**

quiz.question: _______ petroglyph
quiz.explanation: 岩画, 古代岩画. Archaeologists discovered ancient petroglyph in the canyon. 考古学家在峡谷中发现了古代岩画。 || 文化联想：宁夏贺兰山岩画最适合帮助记忆 petroglyph，可以说 **an ancient petroglyph — “The Helan Mountains preserve many ancient petroglyphs carved into rock surfaces by people who lived in the region long ago.”**

quiz.question: slapdash ____
quiz.explanation: 草率的, 草率的工作. The contractor was criticized for slapdash work. 承包商因草率的工作而受到批评。 || 文化联想：中文“豆腐渣工程”最适合帮助记忆 slapdash，可以说 **slapdash work — “Construction mocked as a ‘tofu-dreg project’ suggests slapdash work done carelessly and below proper standards.”**

quiz.question: brash ________
quiz.explanation: 鲁莽的, 鲁莽的行为. His brash behavior offended many colleagues. 他鲁莽的行为冒犯了许多同事。 || 文化联想：“初生牛犊不怕虎”可以帮助记忆 brash 的鲁莽大胆一面，可以说 **brash behavior — “A young person who charges ahead with ‘newborn-calf’ confidence may show brash behavior when boldness outruns judgment.”**

quiz.question: ____ sash
quiz.explanation: 腰带, 丝绸腰带. She tied a decorative silk sash around her waist. 她在腰上系了一条装饰性的丝绸腰带。 || 文化联想：汉服、古装中束在腰间的丝带最适合帮助记忆 sash，可以说 **a silk sash — “A traditional-style hanfu outfit may be tied at the waist with a long silk sash.”**

quiz.question: stash ____ ____
quiz.explanation: 藏匿, 藏匿现金. He tried to stash away cash in offshore accounts. 他试图在离岸账户中藏匿现金。 || 文化联想：中文“藏私房钱”最适合帮助记忆 stash，可以说 **stash away cash — “Someone who quietly hides a little ‘私房钱’ in a drawer is stashing away cash for private use.”**

quiz.question: mesh _______
quiz.explanation: 网状物, 网状网络. The system uses a mesh network for connectivity. 该系统使用网状网络进行连接。 || 文化联想：中国渔民撒开的渔网最适合帮助记忆 mesh，可以说 **a fine mesh — “A fishing net with a fine mesh can catch smaller fish because the openings between the threads are narrow.”**

quiz.question: enmesh __ _______
quiz.explanation: 使卷入, 使卷入丑闻. The politician became enmesh in scandal. 这位政客卷入了丑闻。 || 文化联想：中文“陷入人情关系网”很适合帮助记忆 enmesh，可以说 **be enmeshed in obligations — “An official who accepts too many favors may become enmeshed in obligations that make impartial decisions difficult.”**

quiz.question: thresh _____
quiz.explanation: 打谷, 打小麦. Farmers would thresh wheat to separate grain from chaff. 农民会打小麦以将谷物与谷壳分离。 || 文化联想：北方农村收麦后打麦脱粒的场景最适合帮助记忆 thresh，可以说 **thresh wheat — “After the wheat harvest, farmers traditionally thresh wheat to separate the grain from the stalks and husks.”**

quiz.question: furbish _______
quiz.explanation: 擦亮, 擦亮武器. Knights would furbish weapons before battle. 骑士会在战斗前擦亮武器。 || 文化联想：古代出征前把兵器重新擦亮、磨利和整修，很适合帮助记忆 furbish，可以说 **furbish weapons — “Before a campaign, soldiers might furbish weapons by cleaning rust, sharpening edges, and repairing damaged fittings.”**

quiz.question: refurbish _ ____
quiz.explanation: 翻新, 翻新房间. The hotel plans to refurbish a room on every floor. 酒店计划翻新每层楼的一个房间。 || 文化联想：北京胡同里的老四合院经过整修后重新居住，最适合帮助记忆 refurbish，可以说 **refurbish an old courtyard house — “A family may refurbish an old Beijing courtyard house while preserving its brickwork and traditional layout.”**

quiz.question: faddish _____
quiz.explanation: 时尚的, 时尚的潮流. The faddish trend quickly faded from popularity. 时尚的潮流很快就不再流行了。 || 文化联想：中文“网红打卡风”常常来得快、去得也快，最适合帮助记忆 faddish，可以说 **a faddish trend — “A café designed only around the latest social-media craze may become a faddish trend that disappears within a year.”**

quiz.question: outlandish ______
quiz.explanation: 古怪的, 古怪的服装. She appeared at the party in an outlandish outfit. 她穿着古怪的服装出现在派对上。 || 文化联想：中文“奇装异服”最适合帮助记忆 outlandish，可以说 **an outlandish outfit — “A costume covered in giant feathers, flashing lights, and exaggerated ornaments would look like an outlandish outfit—‘奇装异服.’”**

quiz.question: modish ______
quiz.explanation: 时髦的, 时髦的设计. The boutique featured modish design from Paris. 这家精品店展示了来自巴黎的时髦设计。 || 文化联想：民国上海“摩登女郎”的时髦旗袍形象很适合帮助记忆 modish，可以说 **a modish design — “A 1930s Shanghai qipao with the latest cut and fabric could be regarded as a modish design of its day.”**

quiz.question: prudish ________
quiz.explanation: 过分拘谨的, 过分拘谨的态度. Her prudish attitude made others uncomfortable. 她过分拘谨的态度让其他人感到不舒服。 || 文化联想：旧式礼教对衣着、男女交往过分拘谨的态度很适合帮助记忆 prudish，可以说 **a prudish attitude — “An extremely conservative social code that treats ordinary courtship or modest fashion as scandalous can reflect a prudish attitude.”**

quiz.question: raffish _____
quiz.explanation: 放荡不羁的, 放荡不羁的魅力. The actor possessed a certain raffish charm. 这位演员拥有某种放荡不羁的魅力。 || 文化联想：老上海小说里有些浪荡不羁却颇有魅力的公子哥形象很适合联想到 raffish，可以说 **raffish charm — “A stylish but slightly disreputable young man in an old Shanghai story may possess a kind of raffish charm.”**

quiz.question: offish ________
quiz.explanation: 冷淡的, 冷淡的态度. His offish attitude discouraged friendly conversation. 他冷淡的态度阻碍了友好的交谈。 || 文化联想：中文“爱答不理”最适合帮助记忆 offish，可以说 **an offish attitude — “A shop clerk who barely looks up, gives one-word answers, and seems unwilling to help has an offish attitude—‘爱答不理.’”**
